title: KV + prompt explorations: microbench and eval notes
content:
Quick overview:

This is a scratchpad for a two-day microbench on KV-cache behaviour + prompt permutations against the 7B open model we onboarded last week. Goal: surface surprising latency/throughput tradeoffs when using small-group quantization and when prefix caching is enabled for short-chat workloads. Not polished — notes to self + TODOs.

Environment:
- model: open-7b-a1 (float16 baseline)
- infra: local dev rig (A100-40GB) + dedicated dev node (T4 pooled) for repeatability tests
- serving runtime: local build at commit b3f9d2c (kernel selection tweak for rotary attention)
- quantization tool: qconfig-v2 (per-channel symmetric, group size paramizable)

What I ran (high level):
1) Baseline float16, no caching, batch_size 1, seq_len 64 -> token latency ~ 48ms (p99 82ms)
2) 4-bit per-channel (g=128), no caching, batch_size 1 -> token latency ~ 29ms (p99 54ms), small quality drop on long-range completion (>120 tokens)
3) 4-bit + KV-prefix cache enabled (cache warm) -> token latency down to ~12ms steady-state (p99 18ms), initial token for new convo still 28ms due to cache warm-up
4) 8-bit + KV cache -> similar latency to 4-bit in steady-state but slightly higher memory footprint; perplexity on eval set ~+0.6 relative to f16
5) Group-size sweep (g=64,128,256) showed min latency at g=128; g=64 increased kernel call overhead (slower), g=256 increased quantization error on feedforward weights

Prompt/Chat experiments (short-turn chat workload):
- Prompt pattern A: system + short user prompt (10 tokens) -> good candidate for prefix caching. Observed that caching only prefix tokens (system+static context) gave 1.8-2.2x speedup vs no-cache.
- Prompt pattern B: long dynamic user context (~120 tokens) -> caching had less impact because KV cache dominated by dynamic prefix; still saw ~1.2x benefit in repeated-turn chats where earlier turns reused tokens.
- Prompt variations: using a light instruction template ("You are a helpful assistant.") vs heavy context (document paste) changed token distribution and therefore batch efficiency. Heavy contexts amplify KV memory pressure.

Quality checks (quick):
- Rouge-like sketch on 200 eval prompts: 4-bit g=128 retained ~97% of f16 ROUGE-L for short answers (<40 tokens). Degradation grows for >100 tokens.
- Behavioral glitches: occasional repetition when mixing cached prefix with dynamic system messages — hypothesis: cache invalidation rule bug when system message changes mid-session. Filed Linear RED-345.

Oddities / gotchas noticed:
- On T4 pooled nodes, the p99 latency for 4-bit quant jumped ~10ms compared to A100 for same config. Seems tied to kernel parallelism (fewer warps) and increased kernel-launch overhead. Follow-up: compare kernel launches per token for each device.
- When enabling streaming + KV cache, observed slightly out-of-order token emission for long sequences on dev build b3f9d2c — might be a scheduling race between batch flusher and cache writer. Add tracing around StreamFlusher.
- Memory reporting in console sometimes undercounts KV memory by ~200MB. Suspect accounting vs reserved-alignment rounding.

Commands / quick reproducibility notes:
- baseline run: ./bench/run_microbench --model open-7b-a1 --dtype fp16 --batch 1 --seq 64 --commit b3f9d2c
- 4-bit test: ./bench/run_microbench --model open-7b-a1 --quant 4 --gsize 128 --cache on
- collect traces: ./tools/collect_trace.sh --run-id $RUN_ID --include stream,kv,alloc

Immediate TODOs (ordered):
- [ ] Reproduce cache invalidation bug (RED-345) with minimal script (today) and attach trace (Riley to help)
- [ ] Add kernel-launch counters to the microbench harness (compare A100 vs T4)
- [ ] Try hybrid 4+8-bit profile: attention layers 4-bit, FFN 8-bit (quick patch) — see if quality/latency sweet spot exists
- [ ] Clean up prompt templates used in eval set and push small eval harness to repo (PR candidate)
- [ ] Add a per-request KV-size metric to Console traces to help correlate p99s to per-request cache size

Notes to self / ideas:
- Maybe try a tiny LRU window for dynamic tokens: keep last 64 dynamic tokens in a hot buffer, move older parts to cold storage — could reduce cache pressure for long documents with small returns.
- Consider exposing group-size tuning suggestions in Optimize UI: scan workload seq_len distribution, recommend gsize 64/128/256.

References / links:
- Linear RED-231 (KV rollout plan): https://linear.app/RED-231/optimize-kv-cache-rollout
- Kernel PR that touched rotary kernels: github.com/redwood-inference/kernels/pull/442

End of scratchpad. Will iterate and move useful bits to a proper RFC once reproducible artifacts and traces are attached.
